paragraphs: More people in Ireland now drive electric cars. But charging them in public is getting more expensive.

ESB runs many public chargers. This year it put up its prices two times. A fast charge can now cost 83 cent for each unit of power. That is up to six times the price at home. People with no driveway must pay these high prices.
Electric cars are very popular this year. They are now the top choice for new cars. But Ireland has only 95 chargers for every 100,000 people. The Netherlands has 820.
One expert says Ireland needs 2,000 more charging points in three years. ESB Networks will spend up to €13 billion on the power network by 2030.

paragraphs: Drivers of electric cars in Ireland are paying more to charge in public. ESB, which runs a large part of the public network, has raised its prices for the second time this year.

If drivers use the ESB app, a fast charge now costs up to 83 cent per unit of electricity, and a slower charge costs 70 cent. Charging in public can cost up to six times as much as charging at home. This is a big problem for people who live in apartments or have no driveway.

At the same time, demand for electric cars is higher than ever. This year they became the most common type of new car, with almost 28% of new registrations. However, Ireland has only about 95 public chargers for every 100,000 people, compared with 820 in the Netherlands.

John O'Keefe, the head of the charging company ePower, says Ireland must add more than 2,000 charging points in the next three years. A report by ChargePoint found that the number of charging sessions is growing about 20% faster than the number of new chargers.
ESB Networks says there is enough electricity. It plans to spend up to €13 billion on the grid between 2026 and 2030.

同時，對電動車的需求比以往任何時候都高。

paragraphs: Public charging for electric vehicles in Ireland has become more expensive after ESB, the country's largest charging operator, increased its prices for the second time in 2026. Fast charging through its app now costs up to 83 cent per kilowatt hour, while card payments cost slightly more.

Critics say public charging can now cost up to six times the price of charging at home. That gap mainly hurts drivers who live in apartments or terraced houses without a driveway, because they cannot install their own charger.

The price rise comes as demand grows rapidly. Electric cars have overtaken petrol, diesel and hybrid models this year, accounting for 27.74% of new-car registrations. Yet the infrastructure is lagging behind: Ireland has roughly 95 public chargers per 100,000 people, against 820 in the Netherlands. A report by ChargePoint suggests charging sessions are increasing about 20% faster than new chargers are being installed.

John O'Keefe, chief executive of ePower, argues that more than 2,000 charge points are needed within three years. ESB Networks insists that a shortage of electricity will not hold back growth, and it plans to invest up to €13 billion in the grid from 2026 to 2030.
The Government's strategy promises community charging hubs for people without driveways, but it will not regulate the prices they charge.

透過其應用程式快速充電現在每度電最高83分歐元，刷卡付款則稍貴一些。
批評者說，公共充電現在的費用最高可達在家充電的六倍。
這個差距主要傷害住在公寓或沒有車道的連棟住宅的駕駛，因為他們無法安裝自己的充電器。
這次漲價正值需求快速成長之際。
電動車今年已超越汽油、柴油和油電混合車款，佔新車登記數的27.74%。
然而基礎設施卻落後：愛爾蘭每十萬人約有95個公共充電樁，荷蘭則有820個。
ChargePoint的一份報告指出，充電次數的增加速度比新充電樁的安裝速度快約20%。
ePower執行長John O'Keefe主張，三年內需要超過2,000個充電點。
ESB Networks堅稱電力短缺不會阻礙成長，並計畫在2026年至2030年間投資最多130億歐元於電網。
政府的策略承諾為沒有車道的人設立社區充電站，但不會管制其收費。

paragraphs: Motorists who rely on public chargers to power their electric vehicles are facing steeper bills after ESB, Ireland's dominant charging operator, pushed through its second price hike of 2026. Topping up on a rapid charger via the company's app now costs as much as 83 cent per kilowatt hour.

According to critics, the public tariff can now be up to six times what drivers pay at home, effectively pricing out those who lack off-street parking. Apartment dwellers and residents of terraced streets, who are unable to fit a home charger, bear the brunt of the increase.

The hike coincides with a surge in uptake. Electric cars have eclipsed petrol, diesel and hybrid models this year, claiming 27.74% of new-car registrations. Nonetheless, the network is struggling to keep pace: Ireland has around 95 public chargers per 100,000 inhabitants, a fraction of the 820 found in the Netherlands, and one industry report indicates that charging sessions are outstripping new installations by roughly a fifth.

John O'Keefe, chief executive of ePower, contends that upwards of 2,000 charge points must be rolled out within three years merely to catch up. ESB Networks, for its part, maintains that scarce grid capacity will not stifle growth, earmarking up to €13 billion for network investment between 2026 and 2030.
Meanwhile, the Government's strategy envisages community charging hubs for households without driveways, yet stops short of regulating what they charge.
sentZh: ESB這家愛爾蘭主要的充電營運商強行推動2026年第二次漲價後，依賴公共充電樁為電動車充電的駕駛面臨更高的帳單。
透過該公司的應用程式在快充樁充電，現在每度電高達83分歐元。
據批評者說，公共充電費率現在最高可達在家充電的六倍，實際上把缺乏路外停車位的人排除在外。
無法安裝家用充電器的公寓住戶和連棟街區居民首當其衝。
這次漲價恰逢電動車普及率激增。
電動車今年已超越汽油、柴油和油電混合車款，拿下新車登記數的27.74%。
儘管如此，充電網仍難以跟上腳步：愛爾蘭每十萬居民約有95個公共充電樁，僅為荷蘭820個的一小部分，而一份業界報告指出，充電次數的成長比新安裝數量快約五分之一。
ePower執行長John O'Keefe主張，僅僅為了追上進度，三年內就必須佈建超過2,000個充電點。
ESB Networks則堅稱電網容量不足不會扼殺成長，並撥出最多130億歐元用於2026至2030年的電網投資。
與此同時，政府的策略構想為沒有車道的家庭設立社區充電站，卻沒有進一步管制其收費。

Consequently, rapid charging through the company's application now costs up to 83 cent per kilowatt hour.

Critics contend that public charging may now be as much as six times more expensive than domestic charging. This disparity disproportionately affects residents of apartments and terraced housing, who are frequently unable to install a private charger and are therefore dependent on the public network.

The increase coincides with a considerable expansion in demand. Electric vehicles have surpassed petrol, diesel and hybrid models this year, comprising 27.74% of new-car registrations. Nevertheless, infrastructure provision remains inadequate: Ireland possesses approximately 95 public chargers per 100,000 inhabitants, compared with 820 in the Netherlands, and charging sessions are reportedly increasing approximately 20% faster than new installations.

John O'Keefe, chief executive of ePower, asserts that in excess of 2,000 additional charge points will be required within three years. ESB Networks, by contrast, maintains that electricity supply will not constrain growth, and has allocated up to €13 billion for grid investment between 2026 and 2030.
Although the Government's strategy proposes community charging hubs for households lacking driveways, it does not intend to regulate their prices, which may limit their effectiveness.
